detail: Official counts obtained from six state election authorities: Virginia, Montana, Nebraska, Texas, West Virginia and Wyoming. All six reconcile exactly to their published totals.
Virginia now carries 3,568,674 votes across 133 of 133 localities, against the 23,140 captured earlier. The earlier observation is retained, not overwritten.
FactResultObservation holds 159 observations across two collection rounds. The current-best result tables are derived from it; no earlier observation was edited.
Senator Lindsey Graham died on 11 July 2026; his sister Darline Graham was appointed and won the nomination. The race table is corrected, the original values retained in *_original columns.
All 33 projected winners validated individually across four evidence tiers. 6 are confirmed against an official state source; none now rests on a projection alone.
All 210 ratings carry analysis_eligible = N and are excluded from forecast measures. Rows, sources and the release condition are retained.
Principal committee IDs read from the FEC for all 72 ballot candidates; 70 resolved. Additional authorized committees listed for 15. Leadership PACs excluded.
Added comparability_cohort, receipts_excl_internal_transfers, internal_transfer_share and double_count_risk.
One further ID resolved with corroboration (Nebraska, Chuck Conboy). The remaining 29 unmatched are write-in and minor candidates with no filing found; recorded rather than guessed.
Of the seven v2 High items: two resolved, one resolved for the analytical set, one partially resolved, three retained as unresolved with reasons.
12 open issues with severity, cause and recommended action.
Texas's older official results system opens on the 2024 general election by default. Its 2024 figures were rejected and the current system used instead.
Both earlier versions are unchanged in their own folders. v3 files carry a v3 suffix.
